intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding titin (TTN; 188840) on chromosome 2q31.

checks.claim: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TTN gene encoding titin.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results therefore indicate that TTN mutations are an additional cause of MFM, and that HMERF caused by the p.C30071R mutation in TTN should be classified as MFM-titinopathy.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous TTN mutations shown to cause MFM/HMERF.

checks.claim: The TTN gene is located on chromosome 2q31.
checks.evidence_quote: within a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2
checks.explanation: The abstract places the gene on chromosome 2. The 2q31 band is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is an autosomal dominant myopathy. Onset is insidious in adult life, and the disorder progresses slowly. Patients present with predominantly distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness, and respiratory failure develops while they can still walk (Birchall et al., 2005; Pfeffer et al., 2012). Muscle involvement is highly selective. Muscle biopsies show myofibrillar changes, including F-actin-positive myofibrillar plaques, eosinophilic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles (Edstrom et al., 1990; Pfeffer et al., 2014).

checks.claim: MFM9 is an autosomal dominant myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently described a dominant limb myopathy characterised by early respiratory failure whilst affected individuals were still ambulant (autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure).
checks.explanation: The abstract names the disorder as an autosomal dominant myopathy.

checks.evidence_quote: Early diagnosis and exclusion of this disorder is difficult because of the insidious onset in late adult life
checks.explanation: The abstract states insidious onset in late adult life.

checks.evidence_quote: Respiratory function studies demonstrated a gradual deterioration over time, reflecting the progressive nature of this condition.
checks.explanation: The abstract supports progressive disease with gradual respiratory decline. It does not say the disease progresses 'slowly' overall.

paragraphs.text: Edstrom et al. (1990) described 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with an unusual adult-onset limb-girdle myopathy. Respiratory muscle weakness was a prominent early finding in all cases. In many patients, acute respiratory incapacity was the reason for the first neurologic examination. Other early symptoms were neck flexor weakness and sometimes foot extensor weakness. Electrophysiologic studies confirmed a myopathy, and serum muscle enzyme concentrations were normal or slightly elevated. Muscle biopsies contained myofibrillar plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin, an F-actin marker. On electron microscopy, the plaques consisted of moderately dense thin filaments and were related to Z-disc splitting or extended from Z-discs.

paragraphs.text: Chinnery et al. (2001) assessed 24 individuals spanning 3 generations of a family with an autosomal dominant myopathy, 11 of whom were affected. Muscle pathology was documented in 7 of the 11 affected individuals. The disorder presented in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness. Lung function tests showed progressive global respiratory muscle weakness that was detectable from presentation, with preferential diaphragmatic involvement in some cases. Hip girdle and shoulder girdle weakness appeared later in the disease course. Onset was earlier and progression faster in the second generation. Clinical and pathologic features correlated strikingly. Clinically unaffected muscles showed minimal change. Moderately affected muscles showed fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles. Severely involved muscles had been replaced by fat and fibrous connective tissue. The inclusions were Congophilic and reacted with antibodies to desmin, beta-amyloid and phosphorylated tau protein.

paragraphs.text: Birchall et al. (2005) performed muscle MRI in 7 patients with autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure: 4 males and 3 females aged 37 to 66 years. They described the disorder as a dominant limb myopathy with early respiratory failure while patients were still ambulant. Onset was insidious in late adult life, and muscle involvement was highly selective both clinically and pathologically. MRI showed selective early involvement of the semitendinosus and obturator externus muscles that could not be detected clinically.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2012) studied 31 TTN mutation carriers from 3 families. The disorder presented with predominantly distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness. Onset was highly variable, ranging from early adulthood to a mild phenotype in advanced age. Patients developed neuromuscular ventilatory failure while still ambulant. Weakness occurred earlier and was more severe in the lower extremities, and some patients had axial muscle weakness. Respiratory function deteriorated progressively. No patient developed cardiomyopathy over up to 31 years of follow-up. Muscle MRI in 21 affected patients showed characteristic abnormalities, with semitendinosus involvement in 20 of the 21, including 3 presymptomatic patients. Some muscle biopsies showed eosinophilic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2014) reported 11 patients from 5 British families (F.1 to F.5). Onset was in the fourth or fifth decade, with tripping, falling, myalgia and difficulty walking. Weakness progressed slowly and involved proximal, distal and axial muscles. CK was as high as 1,195 IU/L. Pulmonary function testing showed respiratory muscle weakness in 10 of the 11 patients. Four patients needed nocturnal noninvasive ventilation 20 to 30 years after onset. Features not previously noted in the disorder included scapular winging, which was often asymmetric, elbow and Achilles tendon contractures, and variable spinal rigidity. Some patients had calf or quadriceps hypertrophy. All patients remained ambulant except patient F.2A, who lost ambulation after a disease course of about 25 years. F.2A also had mild left ventricular impairment and palpitations, and patient F.4B had supraventricular tachycardia. Two subjects, F.2C and F.4C, reported only mild myalgias and had mild or very mild weakness. F.2C had reduced FVC, and F.4C had raised CK. Muscle MRI showed early involvement of the semitendinosus and peroneus longus muscles. Presymptomatic patient F.2C already showed the characteristic fatty infiltration of these 2 muscles. Muscle biopsies showed myopathic or dystrophic changes, rimmed vacuoles, and eosinophilic and dark-blue Gomori trichrome inclusions. Six of 7 biopsies showed accumulation of desmin, myotilin, p62 and ubiquitin. In 3 biopsies (F.1B, F.4A and F.5), myotilin aggregates had a characteristic 'cheetah skin' appearance. The biopsy from patient F.4A also showed accumulation of gamma-sarcoglycan and dystrophin.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2014) also described 2 patients with similar phenotypes who carried TTN variants of uncertain significance. Patient F.6 had onset in the thirties with difficulty lifting the lower limbs. This patient had a mildly raised CK (204 IU/L), mild neck weakness, calf hypertrophy and asymmetric scapular winging, with FVC of 52% sitting. Biopsy showed dystrophic features with rimmed vacuoles. Patient F.7 was originally from Brazil and had several affected family members, but none of them were available for assessment. This patient had onset in the thirties, a mildly raised CK (290 IU/L), proximal upper and lower limb weakness, severe ankle dorsiflexion weakness, deltoid atrophy and mild scapular winging. Respiratory function was normal. MRI showed major bilateral involvement of the semitendinosus and fatty infiltration of the tibialis anterior and peroneus longus muscles. Biopsy showed rimmed vacuoles and cytoplasmic bodies.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2014) screened 127 unrelated, undiagnosed UK probands with features compatible with myofibrillar myopathy for the TTN C30071R and R32450W mutations. paragraphs.text: Lange et al. (2005) identified a signaling complex in which the titin kinase domain interacts with the zinc-finger protein nbr1 through a mechanically inducible conformation. Nbr1 targets the ubiquitin-associated protein p62/SQSTM1 to sarcomeres. p62 in turn interacts with MuRF2, a muscle-specific E3 ligase that binds the transactivation domain of SRF. Mechanical inactivity induced nuclear translocation of MuRF2, which reduced nuclear SRF and repressed transcription. These findings link titin kinase mechanosensing to the control of muscle gene expression and protein turnover.

checks.explanation: Patients were recruited at Newcastle (UK) and had a phenotype compatible with MFM.

checks.claim: The TTN g.274375T-C (C30071R) mutation was identified in 5 of 127 UK probands with features compatible with myofibrillar myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing identified the heterozygous g.274375T>C mutation (p.C30071R) in 5/127 unrelated subjects

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation was heterozygous in the 5 UK probands with myofibrillar myopathy features.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing identified the heterozygous g.274375T>C mutation (p.C30071R) in 5/127 unrelated subjects

checks.claim: All 5 probands carrying the TTN C30071R mutation were from British families.
checks.evidence_quote: We report 5 new British families with the previously reported p.C30071R mutation in the TTN gene

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation co-segregated with disease in families F.1, F.2 and F.4.
checks.evidence_quote: The TTN gene changes co-segregated with the disease in families F.1, F.2, and F.4

checks.claim: Probands from the 5 new TTN C30071R families and from 3 previously reported families shared a common haplotype with a 171-kbp core region.
checks.evidence_quote: Haplotype analysis indicated a shared region of 171 kbp between all 8 families with the p.C30071R mutation

checks.claim: The shared haplotype among TTN C30071R families suggested a British founder effect.
checks.evidence_quote: The finding of the p.C30071R mutation in 3.9% of our study population is likely due to a British founder effect.
